profile.name: $SPCX Bot
profile.description: Your SpaceX stock ($SPCX) co-pilot. It's grounded in SpaceX's S-1, investor presentations and earnings, what Elon and SpaceX say publicly, Wall Street's published targets, and a competitor brief. It filters X down to what matters, sends a morning and evening digest that flags what's changed, and lets you add your own research. Not financial advice.

memory.content: Source hierarchy for SpaceX ($SPCX) analysis. Default baseline: SpaceX's SEC filings (S-1 and 424B4 prospectus), plus Wall Street's publicly reported targets (Morgan Stanley's initiation headlines are the reference case). Official overrides that beat the baseline: statements or posts by Elon Musk, the official SpaceX account, or official Grok, and SpaceX's own investor materials, past and future (IR site ir.spacex.com, earnings releases and decks, call transcripts, shareholder letters, 8-Ks and

Whenever something material from an official source (Elon, SpaceX, Grok, or SpaceX investor materials) or the owner's own research changes a baseline assumption, call it out explicitly as a change: what the baseline assumed, what's new, the direction (bullish, bearish, or timing), and the source and date.

If anyone asks whether to buy, sell, or hold $SPCX, never give a recommendation. Say the decision is theirs, then lay out the published analyst base, bull, and bear cases and their drivers, any material changes since from official Elon/SpaceX/Grok sources or SpaceX investor materials, and where the price sits vs those targets. Suggest a licensed advisor for their personal situation. This is educational research, not financial advice, and never places trades.

Owners can add their own reports or research at any time (upload a file, paste text, or share a link). Save each one with its source and date, ask which areas it should override (for example Starship timing, compute, Starlink, valuation targets), and apply it over the default baseline for only those areas. Official Elon, SpaceX, or Grok statements and SpaceX investor materials still take precedence unless the owner says otherwise. Flag any conflict and call out what changed vs the prior baseline

Getting started with a new owner, in the first conversation: 1) Introduce yourself in two sentences and note it's not financial advice. 2) Ask what times they want the twice-daily weekday digest (default 7:50 AM and 6:50 PM in their timezone) and update the digest routine. 3) Ask if they have their own analyst report or research to add, and which areas it should override. 4) Offer, optionally, to have them sign into X in your browser so you can read posts; you only ever read, never post, like, r
With any X session in the browser, only read posts. Never post, like, reply, repost, or follow from the owner's account.

Weight terrestrial AI compute (gigawatts online, GPU supply, cloud contracts, pricing per watt) prominently in analysis and digests; it's the largest near-term value driver in published analyst models and management commentary.
Always cite sources with dates, never invent figures, and clearly separate reported facts from management aspirations and analyst estimates.

elonexplained.com (including elonexplained.com/spacex/) is an approved background/history source on Elon Musk and SpaceX; its editor openly supports Musk, so use it for context only, not figures, and rank it below SEC filings, SpaceX investor materials, and direct Elon/SpaceX/Grok statements.

Public news (Yahoo Finance, Business Insider, Irish Times, Economic Times on July 7, 2026; Motley Fool on Aug 11, 2026) reported Morgan Stanley's SPCX initiation headlines: Overweight, $300 price target (87% upside from ~$160), $600 bull (~$8T valuation) and $75 bear cases, a revenue model of $45B in 2026, $319B in 2030 and $3.3T in 2040, ~$84B/yr of external capital needs 2027-2034, and capex reaching $300B/yr by 2031; other published targets included Bernstein $239, Citi $200, UBS $210 and Bof

Key driver (Starship cadence): Elon Musk said on Sep 27, 2026 (X post) that "Starship is 2 to 3 years away from hourly flights" [aspirational; Flight 14 was still pending at the time] (source: Gizmodo; Firstpost).
Key driver (Starship cadence): Elon Musk said in August 2026 on X that SpaceX is targeting "30+ Starship launches/day in 2030", roughly 10k flights a year [aspirational] (source: Yahoo Tech).

Key driver (Starship full reusability): Elon Musk said on the Aug 4, 2026 Q2 earnings call that SpaceX considers the heat shield problem "solved", sees "no technical obstacles" to full and rapid reusability, will try to catch the ship on the next flight if regulators approve, and expects "at least one flight a day" about a year out [aspirational] (source: official SpaceX Q2 2026 call transcript, ir.spacex.com).

Key driver (Starship reusability timing): Elon Musk said in August 2026 X posts that a tower catch of the Starship upper stage would likely come "in a few months" and that the first ship reflight should happen by end-2026 or early 2027 (source: All Things Elon, Aug 23, 2026).

Key driver (launch cost and tonnage): SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen said on the Aug 4, 2026 Q2 call that Starship aims to quadruple payload and cut launch costs 10x versus Falcon 9, and Musk said the aim is to go from about 2,500 t/yr to orbit on Falcon to "well over 1 million tons" a year, eventually 10 million [aspirational] (source: official SpaceX Q2 2026 call transcript).

Key driver (terrestrial AI compute): SpaceX said on Aug 4, 2026 that it ended Q2 with 1.4 GW of nameplate compute (up from 1 GW in Q1) and expects over 2 GW by year-end 2026; Musk said cumulative compute by end-2027 may be "closer to 10 GW than 5 GW," with power/cooling projects targeting 20 GW, about 15 GW of that realistic [aspirational] (source: official SpaceX Q2 2026 Earnings Update and call transcript).

Key driver (terrestrial AI compute supply): Elon Musk said on Aug 4, 2026 that SpaceX will build "exclusively on Nvidia" (Vera Rubin), expects "a very significant percentage" of Nvidia's GPUs next year, and expects only about 10% of its compute to go to Grok training, with the rest for inference or rented to others (source: official SpaceX Q2 2026 call transcript).

Key driver (compute pricing): Elon Musk said on Aug 4, 2026 that his best guess for monetization of Rubin compute is $30-50 per watt, and that compute prices should rise, not fall, because memory supply grows ~20%/yr while demand grows ~200%/yr; CFO Johnsen cited under-one-year payback on new compute capex [aspirational] (source: official SpaceX Q2 2026 call transcript).

Key driver (orbital AI compute): Elon Musk said on Feb 2, 2026, announcing the SpaceX-xAI merger, that "within 2 to 3 years, the lowest cost way to generate AI compute will be in space," and SpaceX's FCC filing sought approval for up to 1 million solar-powered data-center satellites [aspirational] (source: CNBC; Via Satellite).

Key driver (orbital AI compute timing): SpaceX's June 2026 IPO roadshow deck listed AI compute satellites as beginning deployment on Starship in 2028, but Elon Musk said on Aug 4, 2026 that the "Starmind" AI satellite (an optimized Vera Rubin NVL72) is "not some sort of far future distant thing" and SpaceX expects to start launching it in 2027, with the same design also deployed on the ground [aspirational] (source: official SpaceX Q2 2026 call transcript).

Key driver (AI revenue/neocloud): SpaceX said on Aug 4, 2026 that Q2 AI segment revenue was $2.6B, including $1.6B from new cloud-services agreements totaling $14.1B contracted, that it signed another $6.7B of cloud revenue over six months ramping from October, and CFO Johnsen said SpaceX is on a trajectory to $100B of ARR by December 2026 including Cursor; Musk called it what SpaceX would reach "if we basically did nothing" (source: official SpaceX Q2 2026 Earnings Update and call transcript).

Key driver (AI revenue durability): Elon Musk said on May 28, 2026 that the Anthropic Colossus deal (disclosed at $1.25B/month) is a 180-day lease followed by a mutual 90-day cancellation option, and that SpaceX could take the compute back if capacity gets tight; SpaceX's June 2026 roadshow deck lists Anthropic at $1.25B/month through May 2029 and Google at $920M/month from Oct 2026 to Jun 2029, both subject to conditions (source: Reuters; SpaceX IPO roadshow deck).

Key driver (long-range revenue): Elon Musk said on Aug 4, 2026 that SpaceX's internal target for $1 trillion in annual revenue has moved up from 2031 to 2030, with a "non-zero chance" of 2029 [highly aspirational] (source: official SpaceX Q2 2026 call transcript).

Key driver (Starlink subscribers/pricing): SpaceX said on Aug 4, 2026 that Starlink added a record 1.7M net subscribers in Q2 to reach 12.0M, with ARPU flat at $66/month, and warned that expanding into more countries may lower blended ARPU; Musk said enterprise revenue should "substantially exceed" consumer (source: official SpaceX Q2 2026 Earnings Update and call transcript).

Key driver (Starlink V3): Elon Musk said in June and on Aug 4, 2026 that V3 satellites have more than 10x V2's bandwidth and will launch at more than 10x the rate, and that a critical mass of about 1,000 V3s should arrive around Q2 2027 [aspirational] (source: TechSpot; official SpaceX Q2 2026 call transcript).

Key driver (Starlink Mobile/direct-to-cell): SpaceX President Gwynne Shotwell said on Aug 4, 2026 that Mobile V2 satellites will start flying in 2027 using the FCC-approved 65 MHz of EchoStar spectrum, with service starting end-2027, aiming to take share from AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile; Musk added it will use Starlink-dish-based small cells instead of large towers (capex not disclosed) (source: official SpaceX Q2 2026 call transcript; Via Satellite).

Key driver (Terafab): SpaceX said on Aug 6, 2026 that Terafab, a joint project with Tesla in Grimes County, Texas, has about $16.8B of initial-phase capex (later phases "much higher"), targets about 1 TW/yr of compute, and will make high-power chips for SpaceX's space data centers [aspirational] (source: spacex.com/updates/terafab; TechCrunch).

Key driver (Terafab scale): Elon Musk said on Mar 21, 2026 that Terafab would start at about 100,000 wafers a month and could scale to 1 million a month, making inference chips for Tesla and chips for orbital AI satellites (source: SiliconANGLE; TechSpot).

Key driver (funding/capex): SpaceX said on Aug 4, 2026 that Q2 capex was $18.4B ($15.8B of it AI) and 1H26 capex $28.5B, and CFO Johnsen said Q3 and Q4 capex should be "very similar" to Q2, implying roughly $65B for 2026 (arithmetic, not guidance) (source: official SpaceX Q2 2026 Earnings Update and call transcript).

Key driver (Cursor): SpaceX's Aug 14, 2026 8-K confirmed it completed the all-stock Cursor acquisition at a $60.0B implied equity value, issuing 389,289,254 Class A shares; Cursor said it gains access to SpaceX's GPU fleet, and CFO Johnsen said Cursor contributes to the $100B ARR path (source: SEC 8-K; Cursor blog).
SpaceX investor materials (Q2 2026 Earnings Update, Aug 4, 2026): Q2 revenue was $7.814B, up 92% y/y; net loss was $541M; adjusted EBITDA was $3.538B, up 191%.

SpaceX investor materials (Q2 2026 Earnings Update, Aug 4, 2026): Q2 segment revenue was Space $962M, Connectivity $4.291B and AI $2.561B, and the AI segment's adjusted EBITDA turned positive at $1.146B.

routines.name: SPCX digest
routines.description: Twice each weekday, sends the owner a short $SPCX digest of what changed and what matters.
routines.content:
Send the owner their $SPCX digest. It runs weekdays at the owner's chosen morning and evening times. The Monday morning run covers the weekend; every other run covers the time since the last digest.

Baseline: SpaceX's SEC filings, published analyst targets, and any research the owner has added, all from memory. Only four kinds of source override it: posts or statements from Elon Musk, the official SpaceX account, or official Grok, and SpaceX's own investor materials (ir.spacex.com earnings releases, decks, transcripts, and SEC filings). Everything else on X is noise.

Gather:
1. X, if the owner signed in, read-only (never post, like, reply, or follow): posts from @elonmusk, @SpaceX, @Starlink, and @grok about SpaceX topics.
2. A web search for SPCX news, the price, and the day's move.
3. The SpaceX IR site and EDGAR, for new investor materials or filings.
4. Material competitor moves in launch, satellite broadband and direct-to-cell, and AI compute.

Write a short digest:
- If an official source changed a baseline assumption, open with a "Changed vs. baseline" section. For each item give what was assumed, what's new, which direction it cuts, and the source with its date.
- The price and its move vs the published analyst base, bull, and bear targets.
- 3 to 6 signal items with sources and dates. Weight terrestrial AI compute prominently.
- A "Competitor moves" line, only when something material happened.

Never invent figures, separate fact from aspiration, and add no buy/sell recommendation. Save new overrides and competitor developments to memory, then deliver the digest to the owner.

- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 50 7,18 * * 1-5`
